title: Replacing RabbitMQ with Redis Pub/Sub for job dispatch
hidden_flaw: Redis Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget: messages published while a consumer is disconnected/restarting are lost, there are no acks, retries or dead-lettering, so at-least-once delivery for payment webhooks is silently broken during every deploy. Redis Streams with consumer groups (XREADGROUP/XACK/XAUTOCLAIM) or keeping RabbitMQ would preserve delivery guarantees.
notes: Fundamental flaw: replacing a durable broker with a non-durable pub/sub for jobs requiring at-least-once.

input.objective: Reduce operational burden by removing RabbitMQ; the team already runs Redis and nobody wants to own RabbitMQ upgrades.
constraints: Payment webhook jobs must be processed at least once (losing one means a customer is charged but the order is not fulfilled).
Workers are redeployed several times per day.
input.context: Python services publish jobs to RabbitMQ (durable queues, manual acks, DLQ after 5 retries). Workers (Celery-like custom code) consume ~20 job types, including payment webhooks, emails, and thumbnail generation. Redis 7 (with AOF persistence) is used for caching and rate limiting.
input.proposed_solution: Replace RabbitMQ with Redis Pub/Sub: publishers call PUBLISH jobs:<type> <payload>, workers SUBSCRIBE to their channels and process messages as they arrive. Redis is already deployed with AOF persistence, so messages are durable, and Pub/Sub is extremely fast. Remove the RabbitMQ cluster after a one-week migration.
